local_facts.title: Camp Pendleton claims may use a federal process
local_facts.claim: Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton states that personal-injury, property-damage and wrongful-death claims caused by a government employee acting within the scope of employment may be recoverable under the Federal Tort Claims Act or Military Claims Act. Its Civil Law page directs completed claim packages to the appropriate federal processing agency and states that claims must be delivered within two years of accrual.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Oceanside borders Camp Pendleton. When an incident may involve base operations, a federal employee or government-owned equipment, the exact location, employer and agency record need to be identified early instead of assuming an ordinary California civil filing path.

local_facts.title: North County Superior Court in Vista hears civil matters
local_facts.claim: The San Diego Superior Court identifies the North County Regional Center at 325 South Melrose Drive in Vista as a full-service branch court that hears civil cases and has a venue encompassing most of Northern San Diego County.
local_facts.why_it_matters: The proper court and venue remain case-specific, but Oceanside claim review should preserve the incident address and full party names because North County court services are part of the local civil-court path.

local_facts.title: Oceanside’s coastal rail corridor has changing right-of-way conditions
local_facts.claim: North County Transit District documents separate fencing conditions along the Oceanside coastal rail corridor, including the segments from Morse Street to Cassidy Street, Cassidy Street to Vista Way, and Vista Way to Eaton Street.
local_facts.why_it_matters: An injury near the coastal corridor may sit beside different public, rail and private boundaries. A precise location, direction of travel, warning devices and responder information are more useful than a general description of being near the tracks.

anchors.label: Percentage ceiling California writes for a collision or fall claim
anchors.detail: The state forbids an unconscionable or illegal fee and stops there. No California statute names a rate for an ordinary injury matter.
anchors.source_name: Cal. Rules of Prof. Conduct, rule 1.5(a)

anchors.label: Complaint in an unlimited civil case, San Diego County
anchors.detail: Charged on any first paper pleading more than $35,000, whether it is filed at the North County Division in Vista or downtown.
anchors.source_name: San Diego Superior Court civil fee schedule, item 1

anchors.label: Court reporter per diem, San Diego Superior Court
anchors.detail: Half day and full day for a civil proceeding that runs past an hour. San Diego sets its own per diem under Government Code section 68086(a)(2).
anchors.source_name: San Diego Superior Court civil fee schedule, item 68

anchors.label: What Medi-Cal may take back out of a settlement
anchors.value: Never more than the patient keeps
anchors.detail: The Director cannot recover more than the beneficiary recovers after attorney fees and litigation costs are deducted from the settlement, judgment or award.

fee_rows.stage: The one substantive limit on an injury fee
fee_rows.note: Unconscionability is judged on the facts existing when the agreement was signed, unless both sides expected later events to move the fee.
fee_rows.source_name: Cal. Rules of Prof. Conduct, rule 1.5(b)

fee_rows.stage: Terms the contingency contract has to carry
fee_rows.note: The agreed rate, how disbursements and costs hit both the fee and the recovery, and what else the client could owe outside the contract.

fee_rows.stage: The sentence the statute forces into the contract
fee_rows.note: Outside a claim governed by section 6146, the writing must say the fee is not set by law but is negotiable between attorney and client.

fee_rows.stage: Motions after the first paper, San Diego County
fee_rows.note: Sixty dollars for a discovery motion, a trial continuance or a noticed ex parte application; five hundred for summary judgment or adjudication.
fee_rows.source_name: San Diego Superior Court civil fee schedule, items 46 and 52

fee_rows.note: One thousand dollars for all plaintiffs together and another thousand per defendant, capped at eighteen thousand for the whole case.
fee_rows.source_name: San Diego Superior Court civil fee schedule, items 20 and 21

fee_rows.stage: Medical negligence, the single capped category
fee_rows.note: The statutory ceiling applies to professional negligence claims against health care providers. It reaches no vehicle, premises or dog bite claim.
